A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CAMeLU and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.10. Corresponding material can be matched despite reformatting, renumbering, and additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments across five evaluation datasets, feature-extractor and task-generation ablations, and analyses of representations and learning dynamics.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds results for the task-generation strategy combined with MAML and resource measurements comparing CAMeLU with PsCo.

M1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an adaptation that uses the proposed task generator with MAML instead of CAMeLU's in-context learner. The main CAMeLU architecture, mixing strategy, objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged; the new non-causal terminology clarifies the existing approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data, including ImageNet-964, miniImageNet, and the ImageNet-964/MSCOCO/Fungi combination, and evaluate on miniImageNet, CIFAR-fs, CUB, Aircraft, and Meta-iNat. The added analyses do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds the Proposed + MAML comparison with CACTUs-MAML and UMTRA in Table 8 and introduces PsCo into the resource comparison in Table 11. These extend comparisons using existing baseline names; comparator membership in the original benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The additions introduce a MAML control and measurements of task-construction time, training time per epoch, inference time per task, and CPU/GPU memory. Appendix A.1 also revises the reported CLIP dimensionality specification. Existing splits and training/evaluation budgets are retained, without evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 newly tests whether the task generator benefits MAML, and A.7 adds empirical resource profiling beyond the existing complexity discussion. Earlier ablations remain. The CUB embedding visualization in v3 Figure 2 repeats v2 Figure 4(c–d), so it is not an additional analysis.

E5.justification: v3 adds a general statement about random-seed initialization, without specifying seed values. Three complete runs and mean/standard-deviation reporting were already documented in v2 and remain unchanged. New Tables 8 and 11 provide point estimates without accompanying uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched pre-existing results retain their values. New Table 8 reports Proposed + MAML accuracies, including 31.22 and 41.54 on CUB for one and five shots. New Table 11 reports resource results, including 57 versus 605 ms/task inference time for CAMeLU versus PsCo. These are added results, not improvements over v2 measurements.

T1.justification: The task-collision calculation, task and objective equations, SSIM expressions, transformer complexity bound, and logistic-curve analysis are retained. The non-causal sequence explanation introduces no new formal result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unsupervised task generation combined with in-context learning, strong cross-domain classification without fine-tuning, and efficient inference. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly cautions that CLIP training-data overlap cannot be verified. A.5 adds interpretations about task-generation benefits beyond CAMeLU, their combination with in-context learning, and CACTUs-MAML's alleged leakage advantage. A.7 newly interprets measured resource advantages. The existing A.9 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 promises code upon acceptance; v3 supplies a repository address and reports available code, instructions, models, and pretrained weights. It also revises the CLIP dimensionality description and adds concrete runtime and memory measurements. These are documented disclosures; external resource availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chan et al. (2022) and Singh et al. (2024), expanding the discussion of data-distribution effects on in-context learning and distinguishing CAMeLU's UML focus. The CAML year update and conversion to author–year citations do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions, clarifies non-causal sequence modeling, expands the in-context related-work discussion, and adds a main-text analysis paragraph plus ethics/reproducibility and acknowledgments sections. The overall section order and most explanatory text remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8 and 11 and redisplays the existing CUB embedding panels as main-text Figure 2 while retaining them in the appendix. ICLR formatting changes headers, typography, and placement, with minor diagram-label edits. Existing plots and table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The MAML experiment, resource measurements, specific CLIP leakage caveat, and concrete code/weight access information modestly improve evidence and transparency beyond v2's already extensive evaluation. The gains are limited by sparse protocol details for the new measurements and overbroad interpretation: Table 11 reports higher GPU inference memory for CAMeLU than PsCo, 3224 versus 1630 MiB, despite the general memory-efficiency claim.
